receipt.public_excerpt: CNBC has confirmed that OpenAI expects about $5 billion in losses on $3.7 billion in revenue this year

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI was reported to expect about a $5 billion loss in 2024. That supports the 'loses money' part.

receipt.public_excerpt:
More work is needed to understand
hallucinations holistically, particularly in domains not covered by our evaluations (e.g., chemistry).

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's newest model at the post date still hallucinated on 19% of PersonQA questions, and OpenAI says more work is needed. That supports 'still hallucinates'. The same table shows the rate falling from 0.30 (GPT-4o) and accuracy rising from 0.50 to 0.78, which cuts against 'no sign of getting more reliable'.

receipt.public_excerpt: leading to reduced hallucinations and more reliability across a wide range of topics.

evidence_items.explanation: Four days before the post, OpenAI released a model it reported as hallucinating less and being more reliable, backed by the evaluation numbers in e2. That is a published sign of improved reliability.

receipt.public_excerpt: This is a surprising and important step-function increase in AI capabilities, showing novel task adaptation ability never seen before in the GPT-family models.

evidence_items.explanation: An independent benchmark operator measured OpenAI's o3 preview at 75.7% on ARC-AGI-1, against 5% for GPT-4o. That is a clear sign of meaningful capability gains before the post. The tested model was tuned on ARC training data and differs from the later released o3.

unresolved_gaps: OpenAI's 2024 loss is known only from press reports of a projection, not audited public statements.
There is no agreed threshold for 'meaningfully better', and benchmark gains may overstate real-world reliability.
